text.title: Content Refresh SOP Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when applying Content Refresh SOP. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Detector clauses make them mechanically catchable.

antipattern.symptom: `dateModified` and the byline date move forward; the body diff is under a few percent of words; rankings do not move or drop; readers see a current date above stale screenshots.

root-cause.source: Google Search Central, guidance on page dates

antipattern.root-cause: The refresh was scoped as "update the date and intro" instead of the nine-step checklist; the date was treated as the ranking lever rather than the content.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-refresh-keeps-url-honest-date` and `r-nine-step-checklist-complete`: a refresh without a recorded exit criterion for steps 2, 4 and 6 is rejected; the date changes only when the changelog entry lists substantive edits.

antipattern.symptom: URLs marked `refresh` because Search Console impressions fell, while the rank tracker shows the query itself lost volume or the SERP turned into product listings; the refresh ships and traffic stays flat.
antipattern.root-cause: The scoring dataset had GSC only; GA4 and rank-tracker columns were missing, so intent shift and query-volume decline were invisible.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-one-dataset-gsc-ga4-rank`: refuse to score any row missing one of the three sources; route intent-shifted pages to `leave` or `kill` per `r-three-signals-with-thresholds`.

antipattern.symptom: A cluster of pages is merged into one guide, the sources are deleted, Search Console reports a spike of 404s with inbound links, and topic traffic falls below the pre-merge total.

root-cause.source: Google Search Central, 'Redirects and Google Search'

antipattern.root-cause: The `consolidate` verdict named the survivor but not the redirect map; deletion was executed as the cheapest step.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-consolidate-301-to-survivor`: a consolidate branch is invalid unless it lists every merged URL, its 301 target and the internal-link rewrite.

antipattern.symptom: Killed URLs all 301 to `/`; Search Console reports them under soft 404; the homepage accumulates irrelevant inbound links.
antipattern.root-cause: Belief that any redirect preserves link equity; the SOP allowed a redirect target other than an equivalent page.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-kill-returns-410-never-homepage`: kill means 410 plus sitemap and internal-link removal; if an equivalent page exists the verdict was `consolidate`, not `kill`.

antipattern.symptom: The refreshed page has a new slug "to match the new title"; backlinks now pass through a redirect; the page loses its position for weeks and the refresh is blamed.

root-cause.source: Google Search Central, 'Redirects and Google Search'

antipattern.root-cause: Refresh and migration were conflated; nobody checked the URL column of the artefact against the live page.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-refresh-keeps-url-honest-date`: the artefact's URL for a `refresh` row must equal the pre-refresh URL byte for byte; slug changes require a separate migration decision.

antipattern.symptom: Ninety days after the refresh nobody can say whether it worked; the same URL is queued for refresh again next quarter; the content team's refresh velocity looks high and its lift looks like zero.

root-cause.source: Widely established practice in SEO content operations

antipattern.root-cause: The baseline snapshot and the day-90 re-evaluation were treated as optional reporting rather than as part of the refresh.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-baseline-and-90-day-reevaluation`: the artefact's final step has the baseline snapshot as its exit criterion and a decision branch that re-scores at day 90.

section.title: Human checkpoint
section.p: Before any binding action driven by a Content Refresh SOP output (publish, redirect, 410, sitemap change), a named human reviewer must sign off. The agent surfaces a `ready_for_review=true` flag and does NOT auto-commit decisions, copy, configs, or rollouts.
